sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Per the file, the epoch leader schedule for block production is to be migrated from being keyed by node identity addresses to being keyed by vote acct addresses. Per the file, the expected block signer (per the file) for a given slot is to be determined by the vote acct's designated node identity. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Motivation
paragraphs: Per the file, using node identity addresses in the (per the file) leader schedule means there (per the file) is no straightforward way (per the file) to map a block (per the file) producer to a particular vote acct and its delegated stake. Per the file, this is because the same node identity could be designated by multiple vote accts. Per the file, by migrating the leader (per the file) schedule to being keyed by vote acct addresses, we know exactly (per the file) what delegated stake led to a node's leader schedule slot allocation.

Per the file, this will make certain (per the file) protocol improvements much easier (per the file) to design like how (per the file) to distribute block rewards (per the file) and how to slash nodes that produce duplicate blocks. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Leader Schedule Generation
paragraphs: Per the file, the leader schedule MUST (per the file) continue to be generated (per the file) at epoch boundaries with (per the file) the existing stake weighted (per the file) randomized leader schedule algorithm. Per the file, however, the stake weights (per the file) used in this algorithm (per the file) MUST be adjusted to (per the file) be accumulated by delegated vote acct address rather than accumulating all stake by node identity address. Per the file, as before, delegated vote accts MUST be valid to (per the file) be included in the (per the file) leader schedule generation algorithm. sections.heading: Validator Identity Address Lookup
paragraphs: Per the file, block shreds MUST still (per the file) be signed by the node identity private key and (per the file) block rewards MUST still (per the file) be collected into the node identity acct (also known as fee collection acct). Per the file, once the leader schedule (per the file) is keyed by vote acct addresses, node identity pubkey's will need (per the file) to be looked up by (per the file) loading the vote acct state for the designated vote acct address for a particular leader slot.

Per the file, since the vote program lets updating the node identity address at any (per the file) time after leader schedule generation, the vote acct state from the beginning (per the file) of the previous epoch MUST be used. Per the file, since only valid vote accts are used during leader (per the file) schedule generation, a valid vote acct is guaranteed to exist (per the file) in epoch stakes and its node identity address may be fetched from its acct state. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: RPC Migration
paragraphs: Per the file, existing leader schedule and (per the file) slot leader RPC endpoints (per the file) SHOULD continue returning the resolved node identity address to avoid (per the file) breaking downstream users of (per the file) these endpoints that expect (per the file) the leader schedule to use node identity. Per the file, however, new RPC endpoints (per the file) for fetching the new (per the file) leader schedule keyed by vote acct addresses SHOULD be added. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Alternatives Considered
paragraphs: Per the file, alternatively, the protocol could (per the file) create a strict one-to-one (per the file) mapping between node identity addresses and vote acct addresses. Per the file, however this would require (per the file) quite a lot of onchain program and acct state changes to be (per the file) able to enforce this mapping. Per the file, and migrating existing one-to-many (per the file) relationships is not very straightforward and (per the file) would likely require nodes to manually migrate which could take (per the file) a long time.

sections.heading: Impact
paragraphs: Per the file, negligible impact expected. Per the file, there is to be some extra overhead (per the file) to looking up / caching the node identity address for each vote acct address. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.
